entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Abd Manaf al-Mughirah ibn Qusayy was a Qurayshi and great-great-grandfather of the Islamic prophet Muhammad. He played a pivotal role in the early history of Islam, serving as a prominent figure in the Meccan tribal society. His leadership and influence were instrumental in shaping the social and political landscape of the Arabian Peninsula during the 6th century CE. The Quraysh tribe, under the leadership of Abd Manaf's son, Abu al-As ibn Abd al-Muttalib, resisted the early Islamic conquests, leading to the First Fitna (Civil War) in 656 CE. Abd Manaf's legacy extends beyond his personal connections to Muhammad, as he represents a significant chapter in the early Islamic period, marked by tribal politics, religious tensions, and the eventual rise of the Umayyad Caliphate. The impact of Abd Manaf's actions can be seen in the subsequent division of the Islamic community and the struggle for power that followed the death of the Prophet Muhammad in 632 CE. His story serves as a testament to the complex and often tumultuous nature of early Islamic history, highlighting the intricate web of alliances, rivalries, and power struggles that defined the early Islamic period.
